newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank/Portugal more optimistic on inflation-paper.
newsitem.headline: Bank/Portugal more optimistic on inflation-paper.

text.p: Portugal could end the year with average year-on-year inflation of 3.2 or even 3.1 percent, slightly below the Bank of Portugal's last forecast for 3.25 percent, Bank governor Antonio de Sousa was quoted as saying in an interview on Tuesday.
The forecast would be in line with that made recently by the National Statistics Institute (INE).
"If today we re-wrote the last quarterly bulletin, we would be a little more optimistic in relation to inflation," he said in an interview with the Diario de Noticias newspaper.
The Bank's latest inflation forecast was contained in the quarterly bulletin released earlier in November.
"We are going to end the year with inflation of 3.2 percent or even 3.1 percent, just as INE forecast," the governor said.
De Sousa said that after a first quarter in which the inflation figures would remain little changed, 1997 could see a further fall in the rate from April onwards.
"This year we had the effect of 'mad cow' (disease) which means that we will have the reverse impact of that (next year)," he said.
